issues.issue: The grant of the right to transport oil and gas "from the subject and other lands" across the leasehold, surviving the lease term, cannot be squared with paragraph 25, under which the Lessee agrees not to assert that right unless the lands are pooled. The two provisions give opposite answers on foreign production.

The term is extended so long as gas is "produced or capable of being produced ... in paying quantities, in the judgment of the Lessee"; "paying quantities" is undefined and the Lessee's subjective "judgment" as the measure is open to competing readings. Whether mere capability holds the lease is genuinely arguable.

The paragraph extends the term "as provided in Paragraph 7 following," but Paragraph 7 deals with adequacy of consideration and drilling discretion and says nothing about the term; the shut-in provision is Paragraph 6. The cross-reference does not match the clause it invokes.
"A well shall be deemed commenced when preparations for drilling have been commenced" leaves "preparations for drilling" undefined, so the triggering act is unbounded.

Addendum paragraph 16 defines commencement of operations as entry with equipment to build access roads followed by a drilling rig for spudding, a materially different test, and the Addendum priority clause makes the Addendum prevail. The two definitions must be reconciled.

Royalty is one-eighth of "the price paid to Lessee," immediately followed by struck-through language about post-production costs; whether the deletion forbids deducting gathering, compression and transportation costs is precisely the sort of question the parties would read differently. Subparagraph (A)'s "free of cost" and (C)'s mandatory tax deduction add to the tension within the same paragraph.

The shut-in clause fixes a payment but never states that payment maintains the lease, which must be read with paragraph 2's habendum requiring production in paying quantities or capability of production. Whether shut-in payments hold the lease is left open.

This paragraph reserves "the further right of drilling or not drilling ... as the Lessee may elect," while paragraph 8 provides that the Lessee "shall be required to maintain a well density of at least 1 well per 160 acres" in a unit. Full effect cannot be given to both.

"Lessee shall be required to maintain a well density of at least 1 well per 160 acres contained in such unit" can be read either as an affirmative obligation to drill or as a limit on unit configuration, and "maintain" sets no time for compliance. The sentence is embedded in a pooling clause that otherwise confers rights, not duties.

The density requirement sits against paragraph 7's reservation of the right of "drilling or not drilling ... as the Lessee may elect" and paragraph 20's bar on reading any implied covenant into the lease. Whether it imposes a development duty those clauses deny is a live question.

The Lessor's waiver of "notice of any assignment or transfer of the within lease" conflicts with Addendum paragraph 17, which requires the Lessee to give written notice of any assignment of a 51% or greater interest within fourteen days, and the Addendum is stated to prevail.

"Any damages if not mutually agreed upon" go to three appraisers and "Arbitration shall be mandatory," yet the paragraph enumerates only crop and drainage damages, so the reach of the mandatory process beyond those specifics is undefined. Whether the appraisal is an enforceable arbitration is also unclear.

The Lessor must abide by "all reasonable safety policies of Lessee ... including but not limited to" a single setback rule, leaving the catch-all's reach beyond that one specific undefined and in the Lessee's hands. That is a general-versus-specific problem on the face of the clause.

The surrender clause reduces "the land rental hereinbefore set forth" in proportion to acreage surrendered, but paragraph 3 makes this a "paid up bonus lease" and no land rental is set forth anywhere in the instrument. The reduction has nothing to operate on.

"Force majeure, including but not limited to acts of God, strikes, riots and governmental restrictions" leaves the catch-all's scope beyond the listed events undefined, and the closing words are ambiguous as to whether the lease is extended only ninety days after the event ends.

The Lessee need only "meet or commence to meet all or any part of the breaches alleged" within thirty days, which does not say what discharges the condition precedent to suit. Whether commencing to meet part of a breach suffices is open.

The extension payment is to be tendered "in the same manner as provided in Paragraph numbered 6 hereof with regard to the method of payment of shut-in royalties," but paragraph 6 sets the shut-in rate while paragraph 5 prescribes the method of payment. The cross-reference points to the wrong paragraph.

The integration clause and the bar on any "implied covenant, agreement or obligation" must be read with paragraph 26 and the Addendum priority clause, which incorporate an Addendum that supersedes inconsistent main-body terms. Whether the merger language constrains the Addendum is contestable.

This paragraph and Addendum paragraph 13 both address Clean and Green assessments but in different terms, the Addendum adding CREP and limiting the trigger to operations "on Lessor's lands." The overlap leaves it unclear which formulation controls.

Locations are to be fixed by "mutual consent" with the Lessor's consent not unreasonably withheld, whereas Addendum paragraph 3 deems approval given if the Lessor fails to return the form within thirty days. Deemed approval and mutual consent are different regimes.

The promise not to assert a right to transport gas from other lands unless the premises are pooled contradicts paragraph 1, which grants that transport right "regardless of the source of such production" and makes it survive the term of the lease.

The clause operates only where there is an "inconsistency" with the main body, and several candidates exist — Addendum paragraph 16 against paragraph 3, Addendum paragraph 17 against paragraph 11's notice waiver, Addendum paragraph 8 against paragraph 1's storage grant. Identifying inconsistency is itself the construction question.

Restoration "as nearly as possible" to the pre-drilling condition "within 90 days, weather permitting" gives no measurable standard and no bounded deadline. Both the standard and the weather proviso are open-ended.

"As near its original condition as is reasonably possible" is a looser and differently worded standard than Addendum paragraph 1's "as nearly as possible," and carries no completion date. Which standard applies to the same restoration work is unclear.

Deemed approval by thirty days' silence is difficult to reconcile with main-body paragraph 23, which requires locations to be fixed by "mutual consent" between Lessor and Lessee. A court would have to decide whether silence supplies that consent.

As printed the Lessee agrees not to take water from the Lessor's ponds, springs or creeks "without Lessee's written consent," which makes the restriction circular and self-permitting; the parallel provisions in the other leases require the Lessor's consent. The party whose consent is required is reversed.

The clause survives only as disconnected fragments — "for any violation of any laws or ..." and "the Lessee or those holding under Lessee" — so its operative promise cannot be read. What was indemnified, and against what, is not ascertainable from the text.

The covenant that the Lessee acquires no right to drill an underground gas or oil storage well is at odds with paragraph 1, which grants the right of "injecting and storing, air, gas, brine and other substances from any source and into any subsurface strata." The boundary between the two is contestable.

The obligation is triggered by a "material adverse change in the quality of Lessor's water supply" occurring "during or immediately after the completion" of drilling; neither the materiality threshold nor the temporal window is defined. Both terms would have to be construed to apply the clause.

This paragraph and main-body paragraph 21 cover the same Clean and Green liability in different terms, the Addendum adding CREP and confining the trigger to operations on the Lessor's lands. Which formulation governs is left to the priority clause.

The formula — a "cash equivalency" payment "times the annualized wellhead price" for an allotment of 300,000 cubic feet of gas — does not state a computable amount, since a payment multiplied by a price yields nothing meaningful. The election it offers cannot be valued from the words used.

The clause offers a cash substitute for a free-gas "allotment of three hundred thousand cubic feet" that no other provision of the lease ever grants; the only free-gas right in the instrument is paragraph 8's gas for one dwelling house on a unit owner's land. The entitlement being commuted has no source elsewhere in the lease.

This definition of commencement — entry with equipment to build access roads followed by a drilling rig for spudding — conflicts with main-body paragraph 3, under which a well is "deemed commenced when preparations for drilling have been commenced." The two tests can give different answers.

The duty to give written notice of an assignment of a 51% or greater interest conflicts with main-body paragraph 11, in which the Lessor "waives notice of any assignment or transfer of the within lease." Whether notice is owed depends on which clause prevails.
The provision survives only as the fragment "as ... Lessee," with no ascertainable obligation, amount or trigger. Nothing in the text can be applied as written.

Only fragments of the audit right survive — "have the purpose of determining the quantity of said gas" and "metered and" — so the holder of the right, its conditions and its limits cannot be read off the text.

The provision survives only as the fragment "agree ... that Lessee has not acquired," so what right is excluded cannot be determined from the words. The parallel provision in another lease excludes coalbed methane development absent the Lessor's written consent, but that cannot be read from this text.

If it is the coalbed methane exclusion, it cannot be squared with the main body, which leases coalbed methane gas in paragraph 1, measures the term by it in paragraph 2 and fixes a royalty on it in paragraph 4(B). That would be a direct contradiction of the granting and royalty clauses.
